summary:
Where it stands. This is the final design, with its brand. Four blind judges compared the original Kitchen Table with the final, unnamed and in both orders: all four chose the final (8, 8, 8, 8 against 6.5, 6, 6, 6). Then four more compared the plain final with the branded one: all four chose the branded one (8, 7.5, 8, 7.5 against 7 each) and said its identity is clearly stronger. The thirteen specialist lenses rose from a mean of 6.7 to 7.4 before the brand went in.

The brand: FamilyDB’s own smiling-monitor mark and a wordmark with a lit cursor; Vera’s small screen wherever she speaks; one map of ideas by drive time; phosphor at night. Paper is the family’s, glass is FamilyDB’s and Vera’s. The showcase page has all twenty-four pages and the before-branding switch.
lenses: One “set this up” warning per page, not five
One meaning per colour: yellow only for Send and setup
Person colours by numbered slot, not by name
On the phone, the list before the tools
Atkinson for every word and digit in running text
Draw a real family’s month: long trips, a busy Saturday
Make a surprise impossible to leak
Her own things first; a one-tap “I did it” (a family decision)
Make the phone shell honest: safe area, focus, refresh
“Vera is ready”, so “answering” means one thing
Person colours by slot so a real family can be drawn
Shrink Ask Vera to one row on the phone
changes: The phone is its own layout: a bottom tab bar, lists on the first screen, filters and form options folded away, Plans opening on its list, the chat box pinned. A real system: scales for type, space and corners, one item row, one to-do row, one banner in four tones, one composer, one set of state words; no inline styles, fonts served by the app, one icon sprite, a warm dark mode. Honest pages: one health state per part, said the same way on Home, Status and Settings; reminders shown as unavailable until Telegram is connected; Status leads with money in words. For the kids: their own Home, Chat, To do and Wishes, nothing about cost or how it works, presents never shown, “Ask a parent” where something isn’t theirs, and the line about who can read their chat on every screen. Every state drawn: the daily limit, Vera unable to answer, a reply on its way or failed, Undo after an action, form errors, an empty first day, no results, a busy day, long titles. A written standard (STANDARD.md) for the engineer who builds it.
decisions:
Kids ticking their own to-dos, or rating how a plan went. The app doesn’t let kids change anything today; the kid and parent reviewers both asked for it.

A private chat for parents, so a present can be planned with Vera without the kids seeing it in the family chat.

A kid sharing where they are with a message: hidden on kids’ pages for now.

A twelve-hour clock setting: the design shows “1 pm”; the app needs a setting for it.

Vera stays undrawn, as the style guide decided; the style reviewer asked twice for a character.
